new.title: One row exposure order and decoder thin the optimal paired OR loss at every size of a finite square table
new.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Fin n → Fin n → Bool),
  ∃ order : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
    let exposed := fun h : ℕ => Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => h ≤ (order i).val)
    let cost := fun (h : ℕ) (out : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin n) → Bool) =>
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : Fin n × Fin n =>
        out ({z.1,z.2} : Finset (Fin n)) (exposed h ∩ {z.1}) ≠ F z.1 z.2)).card
    ∃ D : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin n) → Bool,
      (∀ h : ℕ, h ≤ n → ∀ other, cost h D ≤ cost h other) ∧
      (∀ h : ℕ, 1 < h → h ≤ n → h * cost (h-1) D ≤ (h-2) * cost h D) ∧
      (∀ h : ℕ, h ≤ n → n*(n-1)*cost h D ≤ h*(h-1)*cost n D)
new.unlocks: constructs one exposure order and one optimal unordered-pair decoder controlling errors at every hidden size
new.context: Join two distinct labels when their table entries in opposite orientations differ. Expose a maximum-degree label in the current hidden graph. With h vertices and E edges its degree d satisfies hd ≥ 2E. Assign this vertex rank h-1. A decoder uses the reported row if present and otherwise takes the earlier endpoint as row. With one exposed endpoint it is exact, and on each discordant hidden edge it makes precisely one unavoidable error. Thus e_h=E, giving the step inequality. Telescope for h≥2 and treat zero or one hidden label directly.

new.title: A central Hamming band has induced matchings with short binary syndromes and an exponentially small exceptional set
new.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let X := Fin n → Bool
  let wt := fun v : X => (Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin n => v j = true)).card
  let diff := fun (x y : X) (j : Fin n) => xor (x j) (y j)
  let central := fun d : ℕ => 16 * Nat.dist (2*d) n ≤ n
  let tails := Finset.univ.filter (fun v : X => ¬central (wt v))
  let f := 1+(3*n+7)/8
  let vec := fun (x : X) (j : Fin n) => if x j then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  tails.card * 2^(n/512) ≤ 2^(n+1) ∧
    ∃ H : (Fin n → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] (Fin f → ZMod 2),
      (∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → wt (diff x y) ≤ n/16 → H (vec x) ≠ H (vec y)) ∧
      ∀ p q : X × X, p ≠ q → central (wt (diff p.1 p.2)) → central (wt (diff q.1 q.2)) →
        (∀ j, (p.1 j).toNat + (p.2 j).toNat = (q.1 j).toNat + (q.2 j).toNat) →
        H (vec p.1) = H (vec q.1) →
        ¬central (wt (diff p.1 q.2)) ∧ ¬central (wt (diff q.1 p.2))
new.unlocks: packs central pairs and bounds the number of tail masks for a systematic encoder with one check bit
new.context: The two fair-binomial tails outside n/2 +/- n/32 have combined probability at most 2 exp(-n/512). The number of masks of weight at most n/16 is bounded by 16^(n/16)(17/16)^n <= 2^(3n/8). A random binary matrix of the stated height detects every nonzero such mask with positive probability. Equal coordinate sums force equal distances d. Distinct left endpoints of equal syndrome differ in more than n/16 positions. Each crossed distance is d minus that many positions, below the central band.

A random binary matrix of the stated height detects every nonzero such mask with positive probability. Equal coordinate sums force equal distances d. Distinct left endpoints of equal syndrome differ in more than n/16 positions. Each crossed distance is d minus that many positions, below the central band.

new.title: Digit sums and a binary syndrome color every squared-distance bucket on a finite grid
new.statement:
∀ (m b h : ℕ), 0 < b →
  let Q := 2^b
  let X := Fin m → Fin Q
  let width := m*Q^2 / 2^h + 1
  let distance := fun (x y : X) => ∑ j : Fin m, (Nat.dist (x j).val (y j).val)^2
  let bucket := fun (x y : X) => distance x y / width
  let f := 1+m+b*width
  let vec := fun (x : X) (i : Fin m × Fin b) => if (x i.1).val.testBit i.2.val then
    (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  (∀ x y : X, bucket x y < 2^h) ∧
    ∃ H : ((Fin m × Fin b) → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] (Fin f → ZMod 2),
      (∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → (Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin m => x j ≠ y j)).card ≤ width →
        H (vec x) ≠ H (vec y)) ∧
      ∀ p q : X × X, p ≠ q → bucket p.1 p.2 = bucket q.1 q.2 →
        (∀ j, (p.1 j).val + (p.2 j).val = (q.1 j).val + (q.2 j).val) →
        H (vec p.1) = H (vec q.1) →
        bucket p.1 q.2 < bucket p.1 p.2 ∧ bucket q.1 p.2 < bucket p.1 p.2
new.unlocks: prices the syndrome and proves agreement for a tag applied to every possible pair of raw payloads
new.context: Every squared distance is below 2^h times the bucket width W. A difference supported on at most W digits is specified by its support mask and at most W b-bit values in position order. Some binary matrix with 1+m+bW rows detects them all by the union bound. Equal sums and distinct equal-syndrome left endpoints imply their squared distance exceeds W. Each crossed squared distance is the average of the two original distances minus that quantity. Both crosses fall strictly below the common bucket.

Some binary matrix with 1+m+bW rows detects them all by the union bound. Equal sums and distinct equal-syndrome left endpoints imply their squared distance exceeds W. Each crossed squared distance is the average of the two original distances minus that quantity. Both crosses fall strictly below the common bucket.

changed.title: Exact field-linear scan dimension for counting distinct affine-code words that satisfy local truth tables
changed.statement:
∀ (F : Type) [Field F] (k m t d : ℕ),
  let W := Fin k → ZMod 2
  ∀ (base : W) (gen : Fin m → W) (scope : Fin t → Finset (Fin k)),
    (∀ v : Fin k, ∃ j : Fin t, v ∈ scope j) →
    let key := fun a : Fin m → ZMod 2 => base + ∑ h : Fin m, a h • gen h
    let rk := fun S : Finset (Fin k) =>
      let M : Matrix (Fin m) S (ZMod 2) := fun row coord => gen row coord.val
      M.rank
    let need := (Finset.range (t+1)).sup (fun i =>
      let P := Finset.univ.filter (fun seen : Fin k => ∃ before : Fin t, before.val < i ∧ seen ∈ scope before)
      let Q := Finset.univ.filter (fun future : Fin k => ∃ after : Fin t, i ≤ after.val ∧ future ∈ scope after)
      2^(rk P + rk Q - rk Finset.univ))
    let T := fun idx : Fin t => (↥(scope idx) → ZMod 2) → Bool
    let count := fun tests : (j : Fin t) → T j =>
      Nat.card {w : W // w ∈ Set.range key ∧ ∀ j, tests j (fun tested => w tested.val) = true}
    (∃ (s : Fin d → F)
       (step : (j : Fin t) → T j → ((Fin d → F) →ₗ[F] (Fin d → F)))
       (out : (Fin d → F) →ₗ[F] F),
      ∀ tests : (j : Fin t) → T j,
        out ((List.finRange t).foldl (fun cur stage => step stage (tests stage) cur) s) =
          (count tests : F)) ↔ need ≤ d
changed.unlocks: Determines the exact linear memory for counting local tests restricted to a key code, including cuts with disjoint but correlated coordinate sets.
changed.context: Group legal prefixes by their sets of compatible suffixes. Each nonempty set is a coset of the future-only subcode. Equal or disjoint cosets give 2^(r(P)+r(Q)-r(all)) classes. Choose one word per class and pin its past and future projections by local singleton tables. The count matrix on these choices is an identity over every field and factors through the scan state. Conversely extend each class by feasible new coordinates, filter by the current table and add its prefix counts to the next classes. Initialize and finish with one class.

changed.title: Every Boolean square can be rematched into few groups with constant diagonal blocks
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ), 0 < m → m^2*4^m ≤ n →
  ∀ G : Fin n → Fin n → Bool,
    ∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (group : Fin n → Fin (2*(n/m))),
      ∀ (x y z w : Fin n), group x = group y → group x = group z → group x = group w →
        G x (π y) = G z (π w)
changed.unlocks: constructs a rematching and partition with few monochromatic diagonal squares
changed.context: While at least m4^m rows and columns remain, take 2m rows. For each in turn keep columns carrying its more frequent bit. At least m columns survive. At least m selected rows used the same bit, giving a constant m by m block. Pair its rows and columns and remove both sets. The blocks number at most floor(n/m), and fewer than m4^m≤floor(n/m) unpaired rows remain. Pair these as singleton groups. Complementary pairs of equal sizes extend the matching to all labels.

changed.title: Row and column outputs, a shorter cyclic seed and invisible bits give reversible raw-key coordinates at every width
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : Nat), 4 ≤ r →
  let h := (k+1)/2
  let z := k-h
  let u := 5*r-3
  let extra := min (r-2) (z-6*r)
  let seedWidth := min k u + extra
  let rot := fun (offset x : Nat) =>
    ((x <<< (offset%k)) ||| (x >>> (k-offset%k))) % 2^k
  let mix := fun (gap value : Nat) => value ^^^ rot gap value ^^^ rot (k-gap) value
  let chi := fun (word : Nat) => (List.range k).foldl (fun acc site =>
    acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit site)
      (!(word.testBit ((site+1)%k)) && word.testBit ((site+2)%k))).toNat <<< site)) 0
  let step := fun (constants : Nat → Fin (2^k)) (col : Bool) (raw prev t : Nat) =>
    chi (mix (if col then 2 else 1) prev) ^^^ rot (if col then 3*t+1 else 2*(t-1)) raw ^^^
      (constants (if col then r+t else t)).val
  let state := fun (c : Nat → Fin (2^k)) (side : Bool) (key name : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun v tick => step c side key v (tick+1))
      (rot (if side then 3 else 1) key ^^^ name)
  let rowLen := min h (k-u)
  let colLen := min (r+3) (z-u)
  let unused := z-(7*r-2)
  let start := k-(2*r-2)
  let cut := fun (wordAt offset len : Nat) => (wordAt >>> offset) % 2^len
  let seed := fun (w : Nat) => rot (k-(start%k)) w % 2^seedWidth
  ∀ (sched : Nat → Fin (2^k)) (row column : Fin (2^k)),
    let rowPart := fun rowKey => cut (state sched false rowKey row.val) (k-rowLen) rowLen
    let colPart := fun colKey => cut (state sched true colKey column.val) (z+(r+3)-colLen) colLen
    seedWidth+rowLen+colLen+unused = k ∧
    (∀ (label : Fin (2^seedWidth)) (spare : Fin (2^unused))
        (ra : Fin (2^rowLen)) (ca : Fin (2^colLen)),
      ∃! key : Fin (2^k), seed key.val = label.val ∧
        cut key.val (4*r-3) unused = spare.val ∧ rowPart key.val = ra.val ∧
        colPart key.val = ca.val) ∧
    (∀ (original : Fin (2^k)) (change : Fin (2^unused)),
      let mate := original.val ^^^ (change.val <<< (4*r-3))
      state sched false original.val row.val >>> z = state sched false mate row.val >>> z ∧
        state sched true original.val column.val >>> z = state sched true mate column.val >>> z)
changed.unlocks: gives a bijective coordinate description of all raw keys at the stated shortened cyclic seed length
changed.context: Use 5r−3 bits to solve the row pivots downwards, stopping if the cyclic word fills. If a gap remains it begins at raw 3r−1. The available column pivots cover its upper min(r+3,Z−(5r−3)) places. Their longest rightward read wraps back below 3r−1, so no lower unknown is needed at these pivots. The remaining gap starts with the extra seed bits up through raw 4r−4. its remainder is invisible. Prescribe these and the chosen outputs and reverse both sweeps. Estimate 2 to 3 hours.

changed.title: Exact pairing deletion budgets for four-by-four tables of nonsingular anchored binary rank
changed.statement:
∀ (G : Fin 4 → Fin 4 → Bool) (u t : ℕ),
  let bit := fun (i j : Fin 4) => (if G i j then 1 else 0 : ZMod 2)
  let anchored : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) (ZMod 2) := fun i j =>
    bit i.succ j.succ + bit i.succ 0 + bit 0 j.succ + bit 0 0
  let total := ∑ i : Fin 4, ∑ j : Fin 4, bit i j
  let cost : ℕ := if u = 0 ∨ (u = 1 ∧ total = 0) then 1 else 0
  anchored.det ≠ 0 →
  ((∃ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)) (K L : Finset (Fin 4)),
    L ⊆ K ∧ L.card ≤ u ∧ 4 ≤ K.card + t ∧
    ∀ i ∈ K, ∀ j ∈ K,
      Bool.xor (Bool.xor (G i (π i)) (G j (π j))) (Bool.xor (G i (π j)) (G j (π i))) =
      Bool.xor (decide (i ∈ L)) (decide (j ∈ L))) ↔ cost ≤ t)
changed.unlocks: calibrates all four-by-four tables with a nonsingular three-by-three anchored matrix
changed.context: Column permutations act on the even subspace of four bits as the full stabilizer of the all-ones vector w. A complete cut is equivalent to symmetry of the transformed form, with its diagonal giving the shore parity. Construct a nonsingular symmetric form with the same image of w. Rank three precludes an alternating form. For zero budget an invertible two-dimensional minor can be made alternating on three retained labels. Gate-price companions cannot exist for a deletion count.

changed.title: A ternary CNF propagates every forced bit of the two scheduled words, their two names and their common key
changed.statement:
∀ (k r : ℕ), 0 < k →
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc i =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit i)
        (!(word.testBit ((i + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((i + 2) % k))).toNat <<< i)) 0
  let constant := fun (j : Nat) => 3 ^ (k + j) % 2 ^ k
  let first := fun (rowKey rowName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun rowState rowIndex =>
      step (rowState ^^^ rot 1 rowState ^^^ rot (k - 1) rowState) ^^^
        rot (2 * rowIndex) rowKey ^^^ constant (rowIndex + 1)) (rot 1 rowKey ^^^ rowName)
  let second := fun (colKey colName : Nat) =>
    (List.range r).foldl (fun colState colIndex =>
      step (colState ^^^ rot 2 colState ^^^ rot (k - 2) colState) ^^^
        rot (3 * (colIndex + 1) + 1) colKey ^^^ constant (r + (colIndex + 1)))
      (rot 3 colKey ^^^ colName)
  let V := Fin 5 × Fin k
  let word := fun (v : V → Bool) (track : Fin 5) =>
    ∑ j : Fin k, (v (track,j)).toNat * 2^j.val
  let agrees := fun (v : V → Bool) =>
    word v 3 = first (word v 2) (word v 0) ∧
    word v 4 = second (word v 2) (word v 1)
  let B := 17*r+3
  let rounds := 2*(B+1)*(Nat.clog 2 k) + B+16
  ∃ (m : ℕ) (F : Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum V (Fin m)))),
    m + (∑ C ∈ F, C.card) ≤ 256*(k+1)*2^(3*B) ∧
    (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ 3) ∧
    (∀ v : V → Bool, agrees v ↔ ∃ aux : Fin m → Bool,
      PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim v aux) (↑F : Set _)) ∧
    ∀ ρ : V → Option Bool,
      let seed : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) :=
        {l | ∃ raw : V, l.1 = Sum.inl raw ∧ ρ raw = some l.2}
      let advance := fun S : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal (Sum V (Fin m))) =>
        S ∪ {l | ∃ C ∈ F, l ∈ C ∧ ∀ other ∈ C, other ≠ l →
          PEqualNP.Search.negLit other ∈ S}
      let known := (advance^[rounds]) seed
      let complete := fun v : V → Bool => agrees v ∧
        ∀ (raw : V) (sign : Bool), ρ raw = some sign → v raw = sign
      ((¬ ∃ v, complete v) ↔ ∃ C ∈ F, ∀ l ∈ C, PEqualNP.Search.negLit l ∈ known) ∧
      ((∃ v, complete v) → ∀ raw : V, ∀ sign : Bool,
        (∀ v, complete v → v raw = sign) ↔ (Sum.inl raw, sign) ∈ known)
changed.unlocks: Supplies a propagation bound under partial assignments to the names, the common key and both actual outputs in the scheduled adjacency rule.
changed.context: Stagger row-name, column-name and key reads by 3r, 4r and 4r sites. Their histories need 4r, 6r and 7r+3 bits. Each transition fixes both actual output bits and closure identifies repeated sites. In a balanced tree propagate absence of interval paths upward and absence of returning paths through the complement downward, sharing each sibling product. An edge is unsupported if a pin blocks it or its complement has no return. Excluding every edge carrying one sign forces the opposite sign.

changed.title: A truth-table cut of a successful translated-list selector contains a full OR restriction
changed.statement:
∀ (g m r : Nat),
  let A := Fin (m+1)
  let V := Fin g × Fin m × Fin r
  let W := V → Bool
  let deg := fun (b : Nat) (f : W → Bool) =>
    ∃ terms : Finset (Finset V), (∀ mon ∈ terms, mon.card ≤ b) ∧
      ∀ input, f input = (((terms.filter (fun mon => ∀ j ∈ mon, input j = true)).card % 2) == 1)
  let Y := Fin g → A
  ∀ (label : Fin g → Fin m → A → Fin r → Bool) (pick : W → Y),
    (∀ x j i, (fun v => x (j,i,v)) ≠ label j i (pick x j)) →
    ∀ (test : Y → Bool) (base : Y) (coord : Fin g),
      let ones := ((Finset.univ : Finset A).filter (fun z =>
        test (Function.update base coord z) = true)).card
      0 < ones → ones < m+1 →
      ∀ b : Nat, deg b (fun word => test (pick word)) → max ones (m+1-ones) ≤ b
changed.unlocks: Transfers a cut in a jointly selected output label to an OR restriction on actual input bits.
changed.context: Force each other group to return its fixed label. In the remaining group start at a word forcing b from the smaller side. Allow switches only on coordinates assigned to the labels of the larger side. With no switch the test has its value at b. Every nonempty switch set forces a label of the opposite value. Each raw bit is a constant, a switch or its complement. This substitution preserves the degree bound, while OR on the larger side has full degree.
